content:
As of 2025, AI has moved beyond a standalone application category and turned into a core technology layer integrated into business and public processes. Below are the 10 key verticals standing out in this period, where autonomous agents gained operational capability, video generation accelerated, and enterprise productivity was redefined.

1. Autonomous AI Agents

Autonomous agents that can plan and complete end-to-end tasks through API connections have replaced bots that only chat. In 2025, these systems, which became widespread in customer service, sales assistance, and IT support requests, gained browser-based transaction capability with OpenAI’s ‘Operator’ move. According to IBM surveys, 99 percent of developers are working on agent technologies.

2. Enterprise AI

Companies focused on scaling across departments by processing their own data with generative AI. According to McKinsey data, 88 percent of companies use AI in at least one business unit. The Menlo Ventures report shows that enterprise generative AI revenue reached $37 billion in 2025 and that the production deployment rate is higher compared to traditional software.

3. AI Video Generation

Text-to-video generation and automatic editing tools accelerated marketing and content production processes. Nearly half of marketers included these tools in their daily workflow. Large-scale partnerships in the sector, such as the $1 billion licensing agreement between Disney and OpenAI, stand out.

4. Health Technologies (HealthTech)

The use of AI in medical image analysis, clinical documentation, and drug discovery processes is becoming standardized. As of the end of 2025, the FDA approved more than 500 AI-based medical devices. According to NVIDIA reports, 81 percent of healthcare organizations reported revenue growth after AI investments.

5. Finance and Fintech

Fraud detection, risk scoring, and algorithmic trading stand out in banking and finance. 79 percent of major banks in the US have integrated generative AI into their operations. Payment giants like Visa block billions of dollars in suspicious transactions with AI-supported filters.

6. Defense Industry

The use of AI is increasing in intelligence analysis, autonomous unmanned systems, and cyber defense. The US Department of Defense and NATO are expanding their budgets for decision support systems and autonomous projects. Target detection with computer vision and war simulations are at the center of modern defense strategies.

7. Legal Technologies (LegalTech)

Contract review, case law scanning, and document summarization are accelerating with AI. 72 percent of legal professionals use these tools weekly. Large law firms benefit from tools such as Harvey and Lexis+ AI in risk analysis and draft text preparation processes.

8. AI-Powered SaaS

AI assistants embedded in CRM, project management, and office software have become standard. 67 percent of SaaS companies offer AI features in their products. A significant share of enterprise spending is shifting toward these smart features integrated into existing workflows.

9. Vibe Coding

Code generation and management with natural language in software development (vibe coding) stands out as a new approach that increases productivity. According to Stack Overflow data, 84 percent of developers use AI tools. Tools like Copilot and Cursor shorten development times by bringing code completion and refactoring into the IDE.

10. Marketing and Content Production

Personalization, targeting, and media optimization have become algorithmic. 93 percent of marketers use AI to accelerate content production, while 90 percent use it to accelerate decision-making processes. The ad tools of Meta and Google automate creative variation generation and budget allocation.
